sanskrit_verse: अनर्थशीलां सततं तथैवाप्रियवादिनीम् । पूर्वाशिनीं च या भर्तुः स्त्रियं निर्वासयेद् बुधः ॥
transliteration: anarthashīlāṃ satataṃ tathaivāpriyavādinīm | pūrvāśinīṃ ca yā bhartuḥ striyaṃ nirvāsayed budhaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The wise one shall cause to depart from the household a woman who is habitually unproductive, consistently speaks disagreeably, or consumes before her husband.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not mere social role
Causation arises from sustained misalignment with dharmic function
Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of persistent disorder
Restoration logic demands removal of disruptive elements for harmony
Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of relational fields
executable_legal_axioms: IF spouse exhibits habitual non-productivity AND verbal disharmony AND pre-consumption THEN authorized separation
IF behavioral pattern persists beyond three witnessed cycles THEN initiate departure protocol
IF household integrity degrades due to spousal conduct THEN execute realignment through lawful separation
SEPARATION MUST occur without punitive intent AND preserve individual dignity
supreme_court_application: In Supreme adjudication, this verse establishes clear thresholds for marital dissolution based on functional incapacity rather than subjective dissatisfaction. Courts must assess objective patterns over time, ensuring decisions align with preservation of dharma within family units, not emotional reactivity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa confirms that repeated dysfunctional behavior disrupts household dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how unchecked conduct leads to systemic decay. Responsibility lies in recognizing irreversible misalignment. The action of separation serves restoration, not vengeance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process for unresolved relational distortions
Assign responsibility assumption to both parties for mutual reflection
Support capacity restoration through individual spiritual rehabilitation
Reintegrate integrity by establishing boundaries that uphold dharma
final_declaration: Thus spoken by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority of all Dharma. Justice flows from consciousness, not coercion. Separation serves rebalancing, never punishment. Reality remains non-retaliatory; Dharma alone governs.
